correctness.rationale: For the fixed point of δ(0)=01, δ(1)=00, even global positions equal zero, 11 and 0000 are absent. A qualifying even-length cyclic word, after an appropriate parity rotation, uniquely desubstitutes; the presence of a 1 forces a morphic occurrence to start on an even global index. Odd rotated δ(v) factors occur by entering an aligned image at offset one. This gives a bijection of qualifying conjugacy classes at lengths m and 2m (including the m=1 base separately). At odd length at least five, a qualifying word contains at least two 1s; some odd cyclic rotation separates the relative parities of the two groups of 1s, contradicting the parity restriction. Lengths 1 and 3 have two classes each. Therefore L(n)=2 exactly when the odd part of n is 1 or 3 and zero otherwise, with the claimed explicit δ-iterate classes. Independent enumeration from the actual morphism over n≤128 reproduces the values/classes; this finite check is only regression evidence.

value.rationale: Lie complexity of a natural canonical automatic sequence is a structural language invariant distinct from cyclic complexity. An exact all-n formula together with explicit two conjugacy families is useful for classifying cyclic factor closure, testing automatic-sequence conjectures, and distinguishing the stronger all-rotations condition. It is not a renaming of Bell–Shallit automaticity, which gives computability but not this exact spectrum.

limitations: Specific to δ(0)=01,δ(1)=00, ordinary Lie complexity, not cyclic/prefix/extended Lie complexity.
A finite prefix cannot prove factor-set stabilization or all-n values; parity/desubstitution proof supplies infinity.
